subject: Zero-trust keystore handshake for private deployment (VPC / on-prem)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 14 May 2024 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Zero-trust keystore handshake for private deployment (VPC / on-prem)

Hi Alice,

Thanks again for the call this morning. As discussed, Arcadia is planning a private deployment (VPC-first, with an on-prem option later) and wants customer-controlled key material for model payload encryption. I attached a simple diagram (zero-trust-keystore-diagram.png) that shows the handshake we propose so your team can validate the operational boundaries.

High-level ask: can you confirm the following items are acceptable from Arcadia's security perspective?
- Customer retains KMS root key; Redwood holds an operator-facing service account that can call a KMS-unwrap/validate API but never receives plaintext model inputs.
- Operator activities (kernel updates, host maintenance) require a documented breakglass request that must be approved by Arcadia's security contact; requests are logged and audited.
- Subprocessor access: Redwood-managed monitoring agents and cloud storage for ephemeral checkpoints; we can enumerate subprocessors in the DPA.

If that model works, we will surface a short addendum to the DPA that codifies the handshake (key custody, breakglass workflow, and audit log retention). We also want to confirm acceptable retention for operator telemetry (recommended: 90 days) and minimum fields that must be redacted before logs leave your VPC.

I included Kimberly from our security & compliance team on the thread so we can capture legal and technical requirements in one pass. Please let me know if you prefer a short follow-up call tomorrow to walk the diagram.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference

Attachment: zero-trust-keystore-diagram.png (PNG diagram showing KMS in Arcadia account, rewrap/unwrap flow, operator maintenance channel)
From: Alice Tang <alice.tang@arcadialabs.com>

Subject: Re: Zero-trust keystore handshake for private deployment (VPC / on-prem)

Ben —

Thanks for the diagram, that helps. A few clarifying questions before we review a formal addendum:

1) Breakglass: what exact scope of maintenance would Redwood need explicit Arcadia approval for? We need to scope low-risk software updates vs. emergency live-patch for security incidents.
2) Audit logs: can you confirm the fields Redwood proposes to keep (timestamps, operation type, operator id, masked resource id) and what gets redacted? We cannot allow PII or full model payload snippets outside our VPC.
3) Subprocessors: please provide a short list of subprocessors you expect to use for the private deployment (monitoring, metrics, storage) and whether any of them will be able to see metadata that identifies Arcadia tenants.

Also, legal asked whether Redwood would accept a narrow DPA clause preventing any operator access to plaintext model content unless a documented jurisdictional law requires disclosure.

If you can answer inline and send the DPA redline, I’ll get this to our infra/security owners.

Best,
Alice Tang
Head of Infrastructure Security
Arcadia Labs
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Alice Tang <alice.tang@arcadialabs.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 15 May 2024 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Zero-trust keystore handshake for private deployment (VPC / on-prem)

Alice —

Thanks for the questions. Answers below, and I attached an initial DPA redline (DPA_redline_v1_Arcadia.pdf) that implements these points as proposed clauses.

1) Breakglass scope:
- Routine maintenance (non-privileged host updates, scheduled model restarts) does NOT require Arcadia approval; these are covered by the baseline managed-services SOW.
- Privileged actions (manual key rewraps, direct access to KMS key material, or any step that would expose plaintext model inputs outside Arcadia-owned KMS) REQUIRE an Arcadia-approved breakglass ticket. Breakglass must include incident justification, scope, time window, and the Arcadia approver name/email.

2) Audit logs / telemetry:
- Redwood proposes to retain operator telemetry containing: UTC timestamp, operator-id (Redwood employee id), action type (e.g., "kernel_update", "cache_flush"), resource ids (hashed), and outcome code.
- We will redact or never capture model payloads or PII. Resource ids are hashed with a per-customer salt that lives in Arcadia's KMS so raw tenant identifiers cannot be reconstructed by Redwood.
- Retention: default 90 days; we can extend/shorten via contract (we can also push to Arcadia-managed logging endpoint on request).

3) Subprocessors: expected list for the private install is small:
- Metrics: MonitoringCorp (metrics ingestion only, no log payloads)
- Storage: EphemeralStore (encrypted object store for transient shards; customer-managed encryption keys)
- Observability: TraceLite (traces with no payload capture)
All subprocessors are contractually forbidden from writing unredacted payloads outside the Arcadia VPC. The DPA contains the subprocessor appendix and an obligation to notify you before adding any new subprocessor.

4) Narrow DPA access clause: Redwood will accept a clause that operator access to plaintext model content is prohibited except where compelled by a valid legal process. For compelled access we require prior notice to Arcadia where permitted and will push for scope-limited judicial protections (we put proposed language in the redline).

Next steps:
- We can update the DPA per your feedback; Kimberly (CC'd) owns the compliance edits.
- Priyom (CC'd) is our ops lead; he’ll scope a short runbook for the breakglass workflow and the minimal steps an operator can perform during an approved window.

Would you like a 30-minute sync this week to walk the redline and runbook?

Cheers,
Ben

Subject: Re: Zero-trust keystore handshake for private deployment (VPC / on-prem)

Alice —

Short note from compliance / legal ops. Thanks for the thoughtful questions. A couple items we’ll include in the updated DPA redline and runbook:

• Operator-maintenance addendum: enumerates allowed operator actions and those requiring breakglass approval. We will also include a tamper-proof breakglass record (ticket id, approver, signed webhook to Arcadia endpoint).
• KMS integration detail: Redwood will not import or persist Arcadia root key material. All rewrap/unwrapping operations happen inside Arcadia-managed KMS. Where Redwood must call an unwrap API we’ll do so over a mutually authenticated channel and only receive a transient ephemeral token that cannot be converted back to key bytes.
• Auditability: we will provide a signed daily digest of operator actions (hash chain) and can push raw encrypted logs to an Arcadia S3 bucket if you prefer full custody.
• Subprocessor notifications: 30 days notice prior to onboarding anything that reads metadata.

Priyom — please draft the breakglass runbook and include examples of evidence Arcadia can expect to receive (screenshot of KMS audit event, signed operator statement, timeframe).

Alice, if this matches your expectations I’ll ask legal to prepare DPA v1.1 and we can lock a short review call.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
